**Step 1 — Scene:** Stir-fried noodles with sliced meat (likely pork), a few vegetables, and a glossy sauce; a small bowl of mixed fruit; water.

**Step 2 — Vessels:** The plate appears approximately **24 cm** across: area = 3.14 × 12² = **452 cm²**. The fruit bowl appears approximately **12 cm** across: area = **113 cm²**.

**Steps 3–6 — Items, coverage, volume, and weight:** Coverage estimates partition each vessel’s visible food footprint; sauce and oil coat the stir-fry rather than adding a separate footprint.

| Item | Vessel coverage | Area × average height = gross volume | Density | Estimated weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cooked noodles | 38% of plate | 172 × 1.5 = 258 ml | 0.8 | 206 g |
| Sliced meat | 20% of plate | 90 × 0.95 = 86 ml | 0.95 | 82 g |
| Stir-fried vegetables | 5% of plate | 23 × 1.1 = 25 ml | 0.6 | 15 g |
| Sauce | 2% equivalent plate area | 9 × 1 = 9 ml | 1.0 | 9 g |
| Visible oil sheen | Coating, no additional footprint | Approximately 4.4 ml | 0.9 | 4 g |
| Watermelon | 65% of bowl | 73 × 1.9 = 139 ml | 0.6 | 84 g |
| Grapes | 15% of bowl | 17 × 1.9 = 32 ml | 0.6 | 19 g |
| Dark berry/grape | 5% of bowl | 6 × 1.7 = 10 ml | 0.6 | 6 g |

Plate coverage totals **65%**; bowl coverage totals **85%**. Water is excluded from food weight and contributes no energy.

**Step 7 — Energy:** Using cooked/as-served values: noodles 150, meat 240, vegetables 35, sauce 150, oil 884, watermelon 30, grapes 69, and dark fruit 60 kcal per 100 g. This gives approximately **590 kcal**.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **316 g of stir-fry plus 109 g of fruit**, or **425 g total**, is plausible for the visible portions. Meat cut and oil quantity are the largest energy uncertainties.
